source: Gu et al. (2026, ICLR) SimpleToM: exposing the gap between explicit ToM inference and implicit ToM application
finding: Frontier models answer 'does the character know?' almost perfectly but fail to use that to predict or judge behaviour. Reasoning models narrow but do not close the gap.
numbers: 1147 items per question type. Mental state / behaviour prediction / judgment: GPT-4o 95.6/49.5/15.3; Claude-3.5-Sonnet 97.9/67.0/24.9; GPT-4.5-preview 97.0/67.8/26.7; o1 98.6/58.8/32.5; o3-mini 85.4/66.8/41.3; GPT-5 98.5/64.4/40.0; DeepSeek-R1 97.3/73.8/65.8; o1-preview 95.6/84.1/59.5. Random is 50%.
limits: Two-sentence stories, one scenario family, binary questions. Newest models tested are GPT-5 and R1 (2025). No Claude 4+ or Gemini 2.5.
agent_relevance: Answers gap 1 for applied belief use: a reasoning mode helps but knowing what someone believes is not the same as acting on it. Supports a scaffold step that forces belief use in the next prediction.

source: Gu et al. (2026) SimpleToM, intervention section (mental-state reminder, system prompt, CoT)
finding: Reminding the model of its own mental-state answer before the behaviour question closes much of the gap for behaviour prediction. Generic CoT does not. A CoT that names 'what each person is aware or not aware of' works much better than generic CoT.
numbers: Behaviour prediction no-hint -> MS remind: Llama-3.1-405B 58.2->89.5; GPT-4o 49.5->82.8; Claude-3.5-Sonnet 67.0->96.9. Judgment with MS remind: GPT-4o 15.3->42.2; Llama-405B 10.0->25.8; Claude 24.9->84.1. Generic CoT behaviour: GPT-4o 62.8, Claude 77.2; judgment under 40 for all. CoT* (names awareness) behaviour 87.4-92.7, judgment 77.8-86.7. SysP* adds +19.1 to +25.1 on behaviour.
quote: no simple test-time intervention could reliably patch for the lacking applied ToM capabilities
limits: Three non-reasoning models only for the intervention study. Token cost of the reminder not matched to CoT. Gains on judgment are model-specific (Claude large, Llama small).
agent_relevance: Direct evidence for gap 2 (adjacent task). A 'record the belief, then reuse it' step gives about +30 points on behaviour prediction. It does not transfer reliably to the harder judgment step. KaBLE's first-person belief gap itself was not tested.

source: Kim et al. (2025, COLM) Hypothesis-driven theory-of-mind reasoning for LLMs (ThoughtTracing)
finding: An inference-time loop that writes and re-weights hypotheses about one agent's beliefs beats plain prompting, CoT and most reasoning models on four ToM benchmarks.
numbers: ParaphrasedToMi avg: GPT-4o 59.5, +CoT 67.0, +TT 76.0; o1-high 73.0; o3-mini-medium 64.0; R1 68.3; Llama 3.3 70B 57.3 -> TT 71.3 -> TT+CoT 77.0. FANToM all-questions: GPT-4o 11.1, +CoT 40.7, +TT 41.5, +TT+CoT 54.7; o1-preview 44.4; o3-mini-medium 0.0; R1 37.9. MMToM-QA avg: GPT-4o 56.5; +TT+CoT 69.0; o1-high 76.5 (o1 beats TT here).
quote: reinforcing mathematical or programming reasoning does not generalize to social reasoning
limits: Authors' own method. Models are 2024-25 vintage. Only o1 beats TT (on MMToM-QA).
agent_relevance: Partly answers gap 3: an explicit per-agent belief trace helps even against reasoning models. It is a sampling-and-weighting trace, not a Kripke table, so SymbolicToM style is only indirectly tested.

source: Kim et al. (2025) ThoughtTracing, reasoning-model trade-off analysis
finding: Reasoning models are near perfect on false-belief items but drop sharply on the easier true-belief items. Plain CoT also hurts true-belief items for closed models. More reasoning tokens do not predict better ToM accuracy.
numbers: ParaphrasedToMi false/true belief: o1-preview 100.0/36.0; o1-high 97.0/49.0; o3-mini-medium 62.5/65.5 (other o3-mini efforts about 90.5/38.5 and 99.5/28.5); R1 77.0/59.5. GPT-4o 38.5/80.5; GPT-4o+CoT 76.0/58.0. ThoughtTracing ablations (self-correction variant) -5.0, -3.8, -9.0 points.
limits: Over-reasoning on true-belief items is the authors' suggested cause, not proven. Effort-level rows are partly misaligned in the PDF text, so some o3-mini rows are approximate.
agent_relevance: Answers gap 4 in part: the CoT penalty reproduces on current reasoning models as a false-belief bias (assume hidden information even when none). The scaffold should check true-belief cases too.

source: Kim et al. (2025) ThoughtTracing, token-cost comparison
finding: Output tokens of o1 and o3-mini do not track accuracy. GPT-4o with TT uses far fewer tokens than the reasoning models yet scores higher on ParaphrasedToMi.
numbers: GPT-4o+TT and +TT+CoT score almost 10 points above o1-low and o3-mini-low on ParaphrasedToMi. On MMToM-QA GPT-4o+TT+CoT beats R1 and matches o3-mini-medium while using under 50% of the tokens (authors' statement; plotted values not read).
limits: Token figures read from text, not from the plot. TT adds its own tokens, bounded by input length.
agent_relevance: Nearest thing to a token-matched answer for gap 3: structured belief tracing is more token-efficient than free reasoning on these ToM items.

source: Wu et al. (2025) DEL-ToM: inference-time scaling for ToM reasoning via dynamic epistemic logic
finding: A DEL simulator labels every belief-update step of Hi-ToM stories. A verifier (Process Belief Model, Llama-3.1-8B) trained on 20,000 such stories scores candidate reasoning traces. Best-of-N with the verifier lifts all models, most at orders 3 and 4.
numbers: Hi-ToM average accuracy ori -> +PBM: gpt-4o-mini 75.0 -> 93.5 (N=4); gpt-4o 87.0 -> 93.0; gpt-4.1 83.5 -> 90.0; gpt-4.1-mini 78.0 -> 83.0; Qwen3-4B 75.1 -> 84.5 (N=1024); Qwen3-0.6B 44.3 -> 60.0. Order 4 Qwen3-4B 46.0 -> 65.0. Table 2: o4-mini 88.5 avg without PBM; Qwen3-4B+PBM 84.5 beats Qwen3-235B 84.0 and gpt-4.1 83.5. PBM classification accuracy 99.2 (order 0) to 79.9 (order 4). Scores are multiples of 2.5, so about 40 test items per order.
limits: Small test set per order. Trained on Hi-ToM-style synthetic data, so in-distribution. Kosinski-set transfer reported as improved but numbers not read. N=1024 samples is a very large token budget.
agent_relevance: Strongest evidence for gaps 3, 6 and 8: DEL used as a step verifier gives measured gains on nested belief. The gain depends on a trained verifier, not on prompting. Useful as a design pattern (check each belief update).

source: Wu et al. (2025) DEL-ToM, cost and comparison with majority voting
finding: Authors argue majority voting fails on belief-update chains because a wrong intermediate step can win votes, and a step-level verifier avoids this. A small model plus verifier at N=4 is cheaper than the larger model.
numbers: API price per 1M tokens: mini models 2.10 and 0.825 versus 10.50 and 13.75 for the large models (Table 6). gpt-4o-mini gains +18.5 points average and passes gpt-4o.
limits: Majority-voting argument is theoretical (appendix B); the vanilla vs weighted BoN comparison is in a figure not read in detail. Verifier training cost not counted.
agent_relevance: Equal-token caveat for gap 3 stays open: the cost claim counts API price, not total tokens including the verifier.

source: Andrieu and Sileo (2026) Same formulas, different semantics: do language models follow modal logic specifications?
finding: Paired modal problems keep premises and conjecture fixed and change only a frame or domain condition (for example symmetry vs transitivity), with a prover verifying opposite labels. Most models ignore the stated semantics under direct prompting. A reasoning mode fixes this for the one model tested.
numbers: Balanced core, 160 pairs, strict pair accuracy, condition-only baseline 50%, random 25%: DeepSeek V4 Flash 4.4%, V4 Pro 2.5%, GPT-5.6 Luna 21.2%, GPT-5.6 Terra 25.0%, Claude Sonnet 5 65.0%. Flash with high reasoning 88.1%.
quote: four of five recent models perform below the condition-only baseline under direct prompting
limits: August 2026 preprint, one task design. Reasoning mode tested on Flash (and Luna on Frame only). Temperature zero, one response per side. Model names and versions are as the paper states them.
agent_relevance: Answers gaps 1 and 4 for modal reasoning (not belief tasks): direct answers follow a default logic; reasoning mode lets stipulated semantics govern. Opposite direction to KaBLE's CoT penalty. A scaffold should state the frame conditions and force a derivation.

source: Andrieu and Sileo (2026) Same formulas, different semantics, representation and affinity analyses
finding: With no frame stated, models show stable default logics (K or T), but these defaults do not predict explicit errors. Changing the representation (names, relational definitions, TPTP) shifts errors without fixing them.
numbers: Terra strict Frame accuracy 38% with named conditions, 6% with relational definitions, 44% with TPTP (50-pair matched pilot). Best-fit logic: Flash K, Pro T, Luna T, Terra T, Sonnet K.
limits: Small matched pilots (50 pairs). Appendix tables only partly read; the GPT-4.1 rationale-vs-reasoning-mode pilot numbers were not read.
agent_relevance: Supports 'do not hard-code S5': models carry a default modal logic. A scaffold should name the logic it uses for knowledge and belief.

source: Lu et al. (2025) Do Theory of Mind benchmarks need explicit human-like reasoning in language models?
finding: RL on Hi-ToM-style data lifts 0.5B-7B Qwen models far above GPT-4o and DeepSeek-V3 on Hi-ToM, but SFT on the same data does as well or better, so benchmark success need not mean belief tracking.
numbers: Hi-ToM: GPT-4o 69.00%, DeepSeek-V3 70.17%, GPT-4o-mini 58.50%. Qwen2.5-7B-1M base about 40%, RL 84.50%, SFT 86.50%. 4th-order OOD: one small model 23.83% -> 85.83% after RL. In ExploreToM 22% of answers are 'yes' and 4% 'no'.
quote: current ToM benchmarks may be solvable without requiring the explicit, human-like simulation of mental states
limits: Table text in the PDF is misaligned for some rows. Hi-ToM set 600 items. Trained on in-distribution generators. Authors say they did not test o3 or R1.
agent_relevance: Answers gap 9 from a new angle: answer-prior shortcuts in templated ToM benchmarks. Scores on Hi-ToM, ToMi and ExploreToM are weak evidence of belief tracking.

source: Lu et al. (2025) ToM-RL, reasoning collapse and trace transfer
finding: 3B models trained with RL shorten their answers by 88.4% while accuracy rises from 40.67% to 79.17% on Hi-ToM. The 7B model's traces teach GPT-4o-mini to track beliefs.
numbers: GPT-4o-mini with 7B-1M traces: 30.5% -> 91.83%; with conclusions removed 77.33%. 3B traces: 76.17% full, 55.83% without conclusion. Reasoning quality (GPT-4.1 judge): 7B-1M 0.515 -> 0.717; 3B 0.423 -> 0.598; GPT-4o 0.727.
limits: LLM-judged trace quality. Hi-ToM style only.
agent_relevance: A good belief trace is reusable context: explicit per-agent belief traces lift a weaker reader model by 60 points. Supports a 'write the belief table, then answer' pattern.

source: Street et al. (2024) LLMs achieve adult human performance on higher-order theory of mind tasks
finding: On a new handwritten set of order 2 to 6 ToM statements, GPT-4 and Flan-PaLM reach adult level. GPT-4 is above adults at order 6. This contrasts with Hi-ToM, where all models fall with order.
numbers: GPT-4 correct: order 3 94.6%, order 4 73.2%, order 5 82.1%, order 6 92.9% (N=112 per order). Flan-PaLM order 3 94.6%, order 4 78.6%, order 5 76.8%, order 6 71.4%. Humans vs GPT-4 differ only at order 5 (p=.0126, N=565). Overall model comparison N=280.
limits: True/false statements about a story, not open questions, so a yes/no prior can inflate scores. Authors flag possible contamination of BigBench-like text. Models are early 2023.
agent_relevance: Order-dependent collapse is task-format dependent: story-statement checking is easy, Hi-ToM style question answering is hard (gaps 3, 9).

source: Wilf et al. (2023) Think twice: perspective-taking improves LLMs' theory-of-mind capabilities (SimToM)
finding: Two prompts: first filter the story to what the character knows, then answer from that filtered story. Large gains on ToMi and BigToM false-belief items for most models, an oracle filter gives more, and a one-prompt version loses most of the gain.
numbers: BigToM false belief: +29.5 over 0-shot and +14.2 over 0-shot CoT for GPT-3.5-Turbo; slight decrease for GPT-4. ToMi false belief over 0-shot CoT: +16 (Llama2-7B), +19 (Llama2-13B), +47 (GPT-3.5). Oracle perspective: ToMi FB 81.0 -> 96, BigToM FB 70.5 -> 96.0. SC-CoT 33.50% vs SimToM 81.00% on FB (GPT-3.5). GPT-4 +13.4 on ToMi.
limits: 2023 models; GPT-4 saturated on BigToM. SimToM-Single (one prompt) loses much of the gain. Token cost of two calls not matched.
agent_relevance: Perspective filtering ('what does this agent know') is cheap and a good first scaffold step; the gain lives in the separate filter pass (gap 3).

source: Xu et al. (2025) EnigmaToM: neural knowledge base of entity states for ToM reasoning
finding: A neuro-symbolic belief tracker with iterative masking removes the SymbolicToM permutation blow-up and helps most at higher orders (up to order 4) across Llama, Qwen, Gemma and GPT-4o.
numbers: Evaluated on ToMi, HiToM, FANToM with 5 random subsets (100 items each for ToMi and HiToM); example ToMi means 0.828, 0.839, 0.847 for three LLMs. Scaling the entity-state model adds 2.075 tokens and +5.3% on ToMi, but on FANToM adds 21.544 tokens and loses 7.3% (hallucination).
limits: Main table parsed poorly from the PDF; only some means read. No reasoning models tested. Non-reasoning 2024 models only.
agent_relevance: Per-agent belief tables scale badly with order unless masked. Gap 3 on reasoning models is still open: this paper did not test them.

source: Riemer et al. (2025, ICML) Position: theory of mind benchmarks are broken for large language models
finding: Strong literal ToM (predicting behaviour) does not imply functional ToM (adapting to a partner in play). Open models play simple repeated games badly even with accurate behaviour predictions. A DeepSeek-R1-distilled 32B model shows the best functional ToM yet and exceeds its own literal ToM.
numbers: Rock-Paper-Scissors vs fixed partners: Llama-2 70B Chat regret 0.857 vs tabular baseline 0.083; Mixtral 8x7B 0.542. Literal ToM accuracy 92.1-97.4% at the same time.
quote: strong literal theory of mind performance does not necessarily imply strong functional theory of mind performance or vice versa
limits: Game-theory tasks, small open models, mostly 2023-24 models. Single R1-distill case.
agent_relevance: A second angle on gap 9: ToM benchmark scores do not show agents adapt to a person's beliefs. Test in-context adaptation, not only Q&A.

source: Hu, Sosa and Ullman (2025) Re-evaluating theory of mind evaluation in large language models
finding: Position and review paper. Positive ToM results match human outputs on standard items; failures appear on trivial alterations. Humans also do worse on perturbed items (Strachan), so a failure may reflect added task demands, not missing ToM.
numbers: No new experiments. Cites Kosinski 2024 (11 LLMs), Strachan 2024 human comparison, Shapira 2024, Zhou 2023, He 2023 (order effects).
limits: No measurements of its own.
agent_relevance: Gap 9: auxiliary-demand and true-belief controls are now the accepted standard. Add them to any in-house test.

source: Nickel et al. (2026) Understanding artificial theory of mind: perturbed tasks and reasoning in LLMs
finding: Handcrafted false-belief set with five perturbation classes. Accuracy drops steeply for all models. CoT helps overall and its steps are faithful, but it lowers accuracy for some perturbation classes.
numbers: Only Llama-3-70B and DBRX keep limited robustness (50% or more on five perturbation classes) under vanilla prompting; with CoT they meet the 50% threshold in 7 of 10 perturbation classes. Spatial-reasoning perturbations hurt all models.
quote: it surprisingly degrades accuracy for some perturbation classes, indicating that selective application is necessary
limits: Models in the part read are 2024-vintage open models (Llama-3, DBRX). Per-model table not fully read. No reasoning models seen.
agent_relevance: Gap 4: CoT penalty reproduced in Feb 2026 but only on older open models. Selective use of CoT is a design rule.

source: Nguyen, Phan and Gonzalez (2026) Dynamic theory of mind as a temporal memory problem (DToM-Track)
finding: Models infer a current belief well but struggle to retrieve the belief held before an update. Overall accuracy 35.7% (Llama 3.2-3B) to 63.3% (Llama 3.3-70B), random 25%.
numbers: Update-detection 67.5%, post-update 63.9%; DToM-Track questions 27.7% vs standard false-belief 44.7%. Models include GPT-4o-mini, ministral-3-14b and the Llama family. 5,794 items.
limits: No frontier reasoning models in the part read. Multi-turn conversation format.
agent_relevance: A belief table needs timestamps and history, not only current beliefs. Fits the scaffold's need to keep prior user beliefs.

source: Peng et al. (2026, COLM) Communication and verification in LLM agents towards collaboration under information asymmetry
finding: Two agents with complementary constraints in an Einstein-puzzle game. An environment-based verifier that filters candidate actions by affordances, history and inferred constraints raises success for all tested communication settings.
numbers: Human study with 30 participants: silent agents need similar steps but are rated more confusing. Success-rate cells were not read (table layout lost in PDF text).
limits: Not epistemic logic; verifier is rule-based on the environment. Fine-tuned Llama 3.1 agents. Numbers not extracted.
agent_relevance: Adjacent to gap 8: verifying actions against inferred constraints helps under information asymmetry. Not a test of DEL.

source: Suzgun et al. (arXiv v1, Oct 2024) Belief in the Machine (KaBLE), re-check for reasoning models
finding: Only version v1 exists on arXiv (v2 and v3 return 404). Its text has no mention of o1, o3, DeepSeek or R1. The journal version (Nature Machine Intelligence, 2025) was not retrievable, so any later reasoning-model rows were not seen.
numbers: Search of the v1 text for o1, DeepSeek, R1, reasoning model, Claude 3.7 and Gemini 2 found no hits.
limits: The journal paper may add reasoning models; the nature.com fetch was redirected to a login handshake and the article URL was a guess.
agent_relevance: Gap 1 stays open for KaBLE itself. Use SimpleToM (d01) and Same-Formulas (d08) as the nearest 2025-26 reasoning-model evidence.

source: Machery, Stich, Rose et al. (2017) Gettier across cultures, Noûs 51(3)
finding: Crossref abstract only: four cultural groups (Brazil, India, Japan, USA) judge some justified true beliefs not to be knowledge; authors call it a universal core folk epistemology.
numbers: Not read. Wiley PDF and PhilArchive returned 403 or no text. Year corrected from 2015 (b23) to 2017 (volume 51, issue 3).
limits: Abstract level only. Seyedsayamdost SSRN page returned 403. Replication numbers for Gettier cases remain unverified.
agent_relevance: Gap 7 stays open. Low priority for this agent.
